chapter.title: Contractions
chapter.description: Learn how contractions combine two words by shortening them and replacing omitted letters with an apostrophe in informal and standard English.

rules.title: Pronoun + Verb Contractions
rules.explanation: Combine a pronoun with verbs like 'be', 'have', or 'will' by dropping initial letters and replacing them with an apostrophe.
rules.example: I am -> I'm / she is -> she's / they have -> they've / we will -> we'll

rules.title: Negative Contractions
rules.explanation: Combine a verb with 'not' by joining them into one word and replacing the 'o' in 'not' with an apostrophe.
rules.example: do not -> don't / is not -> isn't / cannot -> can't / will not -> won't

rules.title: Question Word Contractions
rules.explanation: Question words can contract with verbs like 'is', 'has', or 'did'.
rules.example: what is -> what's / where is -> where's / who is -> who's

rules.title: Apostrophe Placement
rules.explanation: The apostrophe must always be placed where letters were removed, not where the two words join together.

questions.sentence: ________ (I am) going to the store later today.

questions.explanation: The apostrophe replaces the omitted 'o' in 'not' ('doesn't').

questions.sentence: ________ (They are) planning a surprise party for Sarah.
We ________ (cannot) attend the meeting tomorrow morning.
________ (What is) the matter with the car engine?
questions.explanation: 'What's' is the contracted form of 'what is'.

questions.sentence: He ________ (is not) at home right now.
questions.explanation: 'Isn't' is the negative contraction of 'is not'.

questions.sentence: I ________ (have not) finished my homework yet.
________ (We will) call you as soon as we arrive.
It ________ (was not) raining when we left the house.
questions.explanation: 'Wasn't' replaces the 'o' in 'not' with an apostrophe.

questions.sentence: You ________ (must not) touch the hot stove.
questions.explanation: 'Mustn't' is the negative contraction for 'must not'.

questions.question: What is the correct contraction for 'will not'?
questions.explanation: 'Will not' is an irregular contraction and becomes 'won't'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Who's coming to the party tonight?
Whose coming to the party tonight?
questions.answer: Who's coming to the party tonight?

questions.question: Select the option that correctlyContracts 'let us'.
questions.explanation: 'Let's' is the shortened contraction for 'let us'.

questions.question: What does 'they'd' stand for in: 'They'd already left when I called'?
questions.explanation: Before a past participle ('left'), 'they'd' stands for 'they had'.
